extracted.intended_audience: small businesses and entrepreneurs preparing SBIR/STTR (America's Seed Fund) proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for small, U.S.-based for-profit companies on preparing and submitting SBIR/STTR proposals, meeting eligibility and registration requirements, and understanding program phases and resources. Focuses on procedural steps, eligibility constraints, and where to find assistance and solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the entire solicitation carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you apply, read the entire solicitation carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading the solicitation can prevent administrative mistakes that could disqualify your proposal. Different agencies and solicitations may have specific requirements — follow them exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet all eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you meet all eligibility requirements before you apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility rules can disqualify applicants if not met; consult the full eligibility guidelines (PDF) and confirm company meets program criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit before the closing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Give yourself plenty of time to prepare your proposal. You must respond before the submission closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan timeline to allow for registration, proposal development, and any agency-specific submission steps to avoid missing the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the correct submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply through the agency's SBIR or STTR program before the submission closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each participating agency posts solicitations and has its own submission portal/process — submit via the agency's SBIR/STTR pathway specified in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand agency review process and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Agencies Review Proposals: Review process times vary; check with the specific agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know expected review timelines and that the rigorous proposal review process provides critical feedback to refine your concept; adjust planning accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan strategic use of award funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive funding, be strategic about how you use it, as the award amount may not cover all of your R&D expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a realistic budget and commercialization plan acknowledging that SBIR/STTR awards are often partial support; identify additional funding or cost-sharing if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I purpose and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase I: Awarded companies use Phase I funding to create proof-of-concepts for their innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical Time Frame: 6-12 months. Typical Award Amounts: $50,000–$275,000. Design Phase I work to establish feasibility and generate data to support Phase II proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II objective and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II: The objective of Phase II is to continue research and R&D efforts started in Phase I. Typically, only Phase I awardees are eligible for Phase II awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical Time Frame: 24 months. Typical Award Amounts: $400,000–$1.8 million. Phase II proposals should build on Phase I results and advance toward commercialization-readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III commercialization expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase III: Based on Phase I & II activities, small businesses pursue commercialization in the private sector and/or federal contracting marketplace. No SBIR/STTR funding is awarded in Phase III.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a plan for commercialization that does not rely on additional SBIR/STTR funds; seek private investment, commercialization partners, or federal procurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR partnership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For STTR, the small business must formally partner with a research institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An STTR awardee must subcontract a portion of the award to a research institution. Plan and document the formal partnership role and budget for the required subcontracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit organizations not eligible as direct awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: Are non-profit organizations eligible for SBIR/STTR awards? No. A non-profit organization cannot directly receive an SBIR or STTR award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-profits may participate as minority investors, subcontractors, or sub-grantees. For STTR, eligible research institutions (nonprofit) can be subcontractors to the small business awardee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research institution types for STTR
rubrics_metrics.description: What non-profit research institutions qualify to participate in the STTR program? The research institution must be owned and operated exclusively for scientific or educational purposes, non-profit, and located in the US.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of eligible research institutions include nonprofit colleges or universities, domestic nonprofit scientific/research organizations, and Federally Funded R&D Centers (FFRDC). Ensure institution meets these qualifications before submitting an STTR proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company eligibility specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: You're eligible to apply if your company: Is a for-profit entity located in the U.S.; Has fewer than 500 employees (most applicants have fewer than 10); Is owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some additional restrictions apply with venture capital ownership — review the full eligibility guidelines for details on ownership and control rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity ID (UEI) registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have a Unique Entity ID (UEI) from SAM.gov to receive SBIR/STTR awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and confirm active registration in SAM.gov and possession of a UEI well before submission to avoid disqualification or funding delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 0 and state matching programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional: Phase 0 — Some states have matching programs to cover the costs of creating a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During pre-proposal and preparation phases, explore state Phase 0 or matching programs that can assist new applicants with proposal development expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local assistance and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Find organizations in your area that help entrepreneurs establish businesses, find opportunities, prepare proposals, and bring ideas to market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SBA works with local partners for training, proposal assistance, SAM registration help, commercialization support, and industry networking — contact local assistance early in your planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align concept with agency missions and solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore participating agencies to learn about their missions, priorities, and programs; search all topics to find opportunities that fit your concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Browse agency solicitations and topic areas to select the most appropriate agency and solicitation for your innovation; tailoring to agency priorities increases competitiveness.
